assumptions.obligation: The hardware resets i_rst_n_wr and i_rst_n_rd are asserted together. Once both domains have been released, one reset may not go low without the other. Each reset may still be released at an edge of its own clock.
The writer does not request a write (i_wr_en = 0) while the read-domain hardware reset is still asserted. No operation starts before both resets are released.
The reader does not request a read (i_rd_en = 0) while the write-domain hardware reset is still asserted. No operation starts before both resets are released.

i_full_thr and i_empty_thr are static: they stay stable at every write-clock and read-clock edge while both resets are released. Any value is legal, including values above DEPTH, and they may change during reset.

notes:
These inputs are deliberately left unconstrained because the specification makes them legal and requires the DUT to handle them:
- i_wr_en while o_full = 1 is a legal overflow. The DUT must drop the write and pulse o_overflow (SF-6.3-08, SF-12-01/02/11).
- i_rd_en while o_empty = 1 is a legal underflow. The DUT must drop the read and pulse o_underflow (SF-6.3-10, SF-12-04/05/11).
- Requests while the software reset blocks writes or reads are legal. The DUT must drop them with no pulse (SF-6.3-11, SF-12-07).
- i_rst_n_sw may be driven freely. One low cycle is enough, a longer low level is legal (the sequence stays in HOLD), and a new request during a sequence is served later (SF-3-33/34/47/48, SF-10.7-08/10).
- i_wr_data may be any value.
- Threshold values above DEPTH are legal (SF-9-05).

Constraints that are not expressed here:
- Reset release synchronous to its own clock and a reset held low for at least one clock edge (SF-3-31, SF-6.2-04). These need a global-clock view; the multi-clock harness should model them by changing each reset only at its own clock edge.
- The clock relationship: synchronous clocks from one source with a rational ratio, including coinciding edges (SF-1.1-03, SF-3-23, SF-15.1-02). This belongs in the clock generator of the harness, not in input assumptions.
- Initial reset assertion is already assumed by the harness.

Simplification:
- ENV-01 uses helper flags that only update at clock edges. If a reset is released in the same solver step as an edge, the release may be delayed by one step. This only affects reset timing and does not exclude any functional behaviour.
